citation.title: Stress-constrained optimization of multiscale structures with parameterized microarchitectures using machine learning
citation.version_coded: open-access version of record, publisher HTML

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across stress-constrained benchmarks, multiscale designs used more volume than density-based TO; both approaches had about 1–2% of microstructures above the stress limit.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No optimization-level runtime or speed-up against density-based TO is reported.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and Section 6 emphasize the volume disadvantage; Section 5.3/Figure 26 reports 43% versus 33% volume but better target-displacement error (0.070 versus 0.133) in a multifunctional beam.

baseline.classical_method: monoscale density-based, stress-constrained topology optimization; augmented Lagrangian and MMA
baseline.problem_size: Section 5.3/Figure 26: classical 100 x 50 elements; multiscale 40 x 20 microstructures. Section 5: L-bracket 4096 microstructures, each 64 x 64 elements.
baseline.classical_iterations: Section 5 and Section 5.3: 500 iterations under fixed parameter-update schedule
baseline.training_time: Section 3: 1,000 epochs for each network; elapsed time not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: Section 3: 667 randomized FE/homogenization examples for constitutive model and 6,660 examples for stress model; elapsed cost not stated
baseline.quality_metric: Section 5.3/Figure 26: final volume fraction and L2 norm of target-displacement error; Section 5: full-scale FE von Mises stress and yielded-microstructure fraction
baseline.quality_gap: Section 5.3/Figure 26: 43% versus 33% final volume; displacement L2 norm 0.070 versus 0.133 (multiscale versus density-based).

R1.evidence: Section 5.2/Table 4: primary comparison concerns final design volume and stress constraint, not speed.

R2.evidence: Section 5.2/Table 4: no optimization-level speed comparison requiring an efficient classical timing baseline.

R3.evidence: Section 5.2 and Section 6: no optimization-level speed claim versus density-based TO.

R4.evidence: Section 5 and Section 5.1: returned designs are checked with full-scale FE stress analysis; volume and yielded-cell fractions are reported, and an HS-truss failure to converge is disclosed.

reporting.n_test_cases: Section 5.2/Table 4: three density-based comparisons (L-bracket, double L-bracket, stress concentration); Section 5.3/Figure 26 adds one multifunctional example

notes: Publisher PDF endpoint presented a client challenge, but the publisher's openly readable HTML contains the full version of record. Section 5.2/Table 4 is the first numerical optimization-level comparison in the main text; the HTML renders the table contents incompletely, so the adjacent reported 1–2% yield fraction and qualitative volume direction were coded without inventing table values.
